title: T1: Replace the 7.4 MB Buffer deep-equality pack-immutability assertion
description:
AUDIT REFERENCE: finding F1 / consolidation C1, section 5 and 7 of
docs/audits/test-suite-and-verification/2026-09-14-test-suite-and-verification-audit.md

EXISTING
packages/core/test/contextAssembler.test.ts reads
data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json (7.4 MB) at line 518 and
again at 778, then asserts expect(packBefore).toEqual(packAfter) at 779.

MEASURED COST
toEqual on two 7.4 MB Buffers: 14,354 ms and 2,414 MB peak RSS.
expect(a.equals(b)).toBe(true): 1 ms.
That single assertion is ~12% of the suite's summed file duration, the whole
critical path at any worker count >= 4, and the largest single allocation in
the verification run. It makes contextAssembler.test.ts (3,009 MB, 18 s) the
most expensive file in the repository.

CLAIMED INVARIANT
Assembling campaign-rules context does not mutate the bundled rules pack on
disk.

ACTUAL AUTHORITY
None located. ADR 0013 makes the generated pack the runtime pack; nothing
requires a runtime READ path to prove non-mutation of its source file. The
loader (rules/packLoader.ts via bundledSrdPack.ts) opens the pack read-only
and exposes no write path; assembleCampaignRulesContext never touches the
filesystem. The property is guaranteed by the module boundary.

REQUIRED WORK
Retire the assertion. If the team judges a non-mutation guard still worth
keeping as defence-in-depth against a future write path, do NOT keep the
current form: re-implement narrowly as Buffer.equals, a content hash, or an
mtime check, and site it once in a pack-loader test rather than inside the
heaviest context-assembly test.

ACCEPTANCE
- The 7.4 MB toEqual comparison is gone from contextAssembler.test.ts.
- Any retained guard is O(1)-ish and documents what it guards and why.
- Every other assertion in that test is preserved unchanged.
- Re-measure and record the file's new wall time and peak RSS.

EXCLUSIONS
Do not split the surrounding mega-test here; that is audit T3, not
materialized yet. Change only the pack-comparison assertion.

RISK
Low. If a future path can write the pack, a hash or mtime check preserves the
guard at ~0 cost and documents intent, which the current form does not.
